subject: Generating random integer in model block

messages.author: 82e8106f84fe4fab
messages.subject: Generating random integer in model block
parts:
Hi all,

I've come across a procedure that I can't figure out how to express in Stan code. 
I need to generate a random integer for accessing the rows of a matrix in the model block. However i found that there is no way to generate a random integer in the model block. 

Is there another way I can accomplish this task?

Thank you in advance for any advice

Sincerely,
Adrian

P.S. Pleas find below a simplified description of what I am trying to do. Suggestions on alternative solutions would be greatly appreciated.

I have 2 sets of data which can be used to find the coefficients of 2 regression models. However, the output of the first regression model is used to generate the input to the second regression model. Hence I am trying to generate samples for the coefficients (alpha) of the first model using the first set of data (CapacityRatio as the model output). I would then like to use these samples in the second model by randomly sampling from them and using them to compute the input to the second regression model. The intention is to generate the posterior distribution of both models but by first constraining the coefficients of the first regression model since I have data for those as well. 

First Model:
data {
int<lower=0> K;
vector[K] temperature;
vector[K] capacityRatio;
}

parameters {
vector[2] alpha;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}

model {
capacityRatio ~ normal(alpha[1] + alpha[2] * temperature);
}

Second Model:
data {
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=0> K; # number of samples from first model
real<lower=0> nominalCapacity;
vector[N] temperature;
matrix[K,2] alpha; # 1st col is alpha[1] and 2nd is alpha[2];
vector[N] measuredPower;
}

parameters {
vector[2] beta;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}

model {
vector[N] predictedPower;
real capacityRatio;
real partLoadRatio;
int RandomIdx; # How to generate a random index to access row of matrix[K,2] alpha

for (i in 1:N) {
capacityRatio <- alpha[RandomIdx,1] + alpha[RandomIdx,2] * temperature[i];
partLoadRatio <- load[i] / (capacityRatio * nominalCapacity);
preditedPower[i] <- beta[1] + beta[2] * partLoadRatio;
}
measuredPower ~ normal(predictedPower,sigma);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generating random integer in model block
parts:
You're right. There's no good way to compute a random integer
in the model block. That's on purpose, as it breaks differentiability
for our HMC methods.

What you're proposing corresponds to what BUGS called "cut". We
don't want to do that, either, as it's not the right Bayesian model
(precisely because the cut makes info flow only one way). The best
you could do is run the second model for each of the first model
values. Still a cut, and still not Bayesian, but it'll compute.

The Bayesian alternative is to build a joint model and fit both
at the same time.

- Bob
